I've resolved all 97 patterns to their source files. Now I'm writing the small loop that sends them to the Kimi seats.㊥ Gist: All five Kimi seats are now reading the 97 patterns, ten to a pack. Each answer is checked before it's accepted: the stage and kind must come from the rubric's lists, and the quote must appear word for word in the pattern's source. I'm parked on the first five packs, and when they finish I'll read a sample of the labels against their sources and report back. The loop handles the remaining packs itself, and should finish in well under an hour.

㊢ (setup)
- **The loop:** `futon0/analysis/audits/pattern_stage_read_loop.py`, committed as futon0 `31b097b`.
- **What each pack contains:** the rubric, plus the full text of each of its ten patterns. The ten patterns stored in `.multiarg` files get just their own section.
- **The rubric:** the eight stage glosses that the 689 existing labels use, transcribed from their rationales. The rest is the method note's rules: label from the pattern's own text, never from its directory, and treat maths techniques as subject.
- **Retries:** a refused answer is retried once.
- **Where accepted labels go:** `pattern-stage-additions-2026-10-01.jsonl`, with each source's path and sha256. The 21 September file is not touched.

㊬ (the checker, tested before launch) All 97 patterns resolved to a source. A correct quote was accepted. A made-up quote was refused as "not verbatim", and an invented kind ("habit") was refused too.

🈖 (watching it)
- **Progress:** `tail -f ~/code/futon0/analysis/audits/pattern-stage-read-loop.log.jsonl` shows one line per pack, with the number accepted and the reasons for any refusals.
- **Stop:** `touch /tmp/claude17/pattern-stage-read.STOP`
- **Loop process:** `bg-1790889916673-6`.
- **My park:** `park-a63469ef-…`, waiting on the first five jobs, with a 45-minute deadline.

🈝 (afterwards) Once all 97 are in, rebuilding the stage table and figure for 22 August to today is the next step. That rebuild will also drop the 92 notices that the Minard filter misses.

㊥ Gist: 90 of the 97 patterns are labelled and the last pack is still running. Every answer passed the checker, so nothing has been refused. In a sample of five labels, two clearly fit their pattern and three are arguable, including the most-hit one. That's about what you'd expect from labels still marked "provisional pending your blind check".

㊬ (five labels read against their source)
- **Agree:**
  - `translation/test-by-reproducing-behaviour` → practice/assurance. It quotes "A test the wrong translation would also pass shows nothing".
  - `math-strategy/hypothesis-category-check` → practice/assurance. It's a proof audit discipline, which the rubric allows as practice.
- **Arguable:**
  - `test-registry/bind-the-subject` (13 hits) → believe. Its own conclusion says "the whole readout is evidence, never a gate". Its sibling `judge-adequacy` is labelled assurance, and I'd have chosen assurance here too.
  - `snatch/use-talk-to-make-a-testable-offer` → practice/assurance. It's strategy for one game, so I'd call it subject, and arguably evaluate.
  - `plos-npt…/quote-table-not-quote-flood` → subject/perceive. It's a writing technique, so I'd say act or none. Perceive is a stretch.

㊟ (two things to watch)
- **No "mixed" labels:** of the 80 checked, 52 are practice and 28 subject. The original 689 had 13% mixed.
- **Pace:** packs came back in 1–2.7 minutes each, faster than the backfill packs, which is the corner-cutting signal from `batch-packets-invite-corner-cutting`. Every quote is verbatim, though, so each pattern was opened.

On this sample about one label in two or three could reasonably differ. Each one shifts that pattern's hits between stages, which matters most for `bind-the-subject`.

㊭ (next) When the last pack lands, I'll send out the rebuild of the stage table and figure for 22 August to today. It uses the 21 September labels plus these additions, adds the `xiang2000_p6o3` filter, and moves the hard-coded end date. The changed labels for the 1,255 new hits are marked as such in the table. If you'd like to correct `bind-the-subject` before the rebuild, say which stage and I'll make the edit by hand.

previous_reply_acts.text: Gist: The Minard method does have a built-in guess for this, a stage prior for each library directory. But the guess is poor. When I scored it against the 689 hand labels, the directory prior matched only 36% of patterns, and a leave-one-out majority vote within each directory matched 35%. Always answering the most common stage would score 21%, so inferring from the directory gives a stage table that is about two-thirds wrong for those patterns. I'd have a Kimi seat read the 97 instead, which is how the original labels were made.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what I measured just now)
- **Directory prior (`pattern-stage-dir-priors-2026-09-21.edn`):** matches the hand label on 248 of 684 patterns, 38% when weighted by hits.
- **Leave-one-out majority of labelled siblings:** 237 of 670 (35%).
- **Coverage of the 97:** 90 have labelled siblings, 5 have only a prior, and 2 have neither.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (labelling is already a model reading) The 689 existing labels weren't made by hand: agents read each pattern's source text and quoted the line that justified the choice. They are still "provisional pending Joe's blind check". So reading the 97 the same way isn't extra rigour, it's simply the method. A Kimi pack of ten patterns, each with its IF/THEN text inlined, takes about 5 minutes. Ten packs on the five Kimi seats would take under half an hour.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (an inference that might work) The patterns already have embeddings in futon3a, so each new pattern could take the stage of its nearest labelled neighbours. I haven't tested it. It is worth using only if a leave-one-out score on the 689 comes out well above the directory's 35%, which is a quick check if you'd prefer inference to reading.
